subject: art-design
topicDisplay: Art Craft And Design Mixed Media
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Jackson Pollock is famous for which technique?
options: Dripping and pouring paint onto canvas
questions.explain: Jackson Pollock developed a 'drip' technique, pouring paint onto canvas laid on the floor.

questions.q: In weaving, the threads held under tension on the loom that run lengthways are the...
questions.explain: The warp threads run lengthways and are held taut on the loom while the weft is woven across them.

questions.q: What is cross-hatching?
options: Two sets of parallel lines crossing to build darker tone
Dotting the surface to suggest tone
questions.explain: Cross-hatching layers a second set of lines across the first to create darker, denser tone.

questions.q: What is 'slip' in pottery?
options: Liquid clay used to join pieces or decorate
questions.explain: Slip is clay mixed with water to a creamy liquid, used as a glue or for decoration.

questions.q: A graphite pencil labelled '6B' is...
questions.explain: The 'B' scale denotes softer, darker pencils, so 6B is much softer and darker than an H grade.

questions.q: Which is an example of three-dimensional design in everyday life?
options: A product such as a chair
questions.explain: Product design, such as a chair, is a form of three-dimensional design.

questions.q: 'Distressing' fabric in textiles means...
options: Deliberately fraying, tearing or wearing it for effect
questions.explain: Distressing intentionally frays, tears or ages fabric to create texture and a worn look.

questions.q: What does adding black to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding black to a colour produces a shade (a darker version), whereas adding white produces a tint.

questions.q: Increasing the 'contrast' of a photo does what?
options: Makes darks darker and lights lighter
questions.explain: Increasing contrast widens the difference between the lightest and darkest tones.

questions.q: In photography, 'cropping' an image means...
options: Cutting away parts of the frame to improve composition
questions.explain: Cropping removes unwanted edges to tighten or rebalance the composition.

questions.q: Which drawing medium is best for soft, smudgeable, very dark marks?
questions.explain: Charcoal produces rich, dark, easily smudged marks ideal for tonal drawing.

questions.q: 'Saturation' in an image describes...
options: The intensity or purity of the colours
questions.explain: Saturation measures how vivid or intense the colours are; low saturation looks washed out.

questions.q: Which assessment objective involves responding to the work of other artists?
options: Developing ideas through investigation of sources
questions.explain: Developing ideas requires investigating sources, including the work of relevant artists and cultures.

questions.q: Bonding (interfacing) fabric with heat from an iron usually relies on...
options: A glue web or adhesive that melts
questions.explain: Bondaweb and fusible interfacing carry a heat-activated adhesive that melts to join fabrics.

questions.q: Salvador Dali is associated with which art movement?
questions.explain: Salvador Dali was a leading Surrealist, known for dream-like works such as his melting clocks.

questions.q: Batik is a textile technique that uses what to resist dye?
questions.explain: In batik, hot wax is applied to fabric so the waxed areas resist the dye.

questions.q: Which material is shaped while soft and then fired hard in a kiln?
questions.explain: Clay is modelled while soft, then fired in a kiln to become hard and permanent.

questions.q: Vincent van Gogh is associated with which movement, known for expressive colour and brushwork?
questions.explain: Van Gogh was a Post-Impressionist, using bold colour and energetic brushstrokes to convey emotion.

questions.q: What does ISO measure on a camera?
questions.explain: ISO sets the sensor's sensitivity to light; a high ISO brightens images but can add noise.

questions.q: 'The exposure triangle' refers to the relationship between...
questions.explain: Aperture, shutter speed and ISO together control exposure and form the exposure triangle.

questions.q: Why might a photographer use editing 'layers'?
options: To reduce the file to one flat image instantly
To stack and adjust separate elements independently
questions.explain: Layers let an editor stack and adjust separate elements without permanently altering the others.

questions.q: 'Devore' (burnout) is a technique that...
options: Uses a chemical to dissolve fibres and leave a sheer pattern
questions.explain: Devore applies a chemical paste that burns away certain fibres, leaving a sheer patterned effect.
